title: A Thermodynamic Analysis of Enhanced Metastability in Isochoric Supercooled Liquids
content:
Isochoric confinement converts incipient solidification into a self-limiting thermodynamic feedback: expansion raises pressure, the negative Clapeyron slope depresses the melting temperature, and the effective supercooling and nucleation driving force decrease. A geometry-independent stability number, built only from bulk material properties, quantifies this effect and guides cryopreservation solution design.


ABSTRACT

Supercooled liquids with negative Clapeyron slopes are more stable at constant volume than at constant pressure. We compare the isochoric and isobaric driving forces for incipient solidification via a first-order perturbation expansion of the thermodynamic potentials in the solid mass fraction. The analysis yields a geometry-independent inequality: the isochoric Helmholtz driving force is strictly smaller than the isobaric Gibbs driving force. It also introduces a dimensionless stability number Π 0 = (vs−vl)2/(Lf·κl·vl)$({{{v}_{\mathrm{s}}} - {{v}_{\mathrm{l}}}})^{2}/({{{L}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\cdot}{{\kappa}_{\mathrm{l}}}{\cdot}{{v}_{\mathrm{l}}}})$, where vs${{v}_{\mathrm{s}}}$ and vl${{v}_{\mathrm{l}}}$ are the solid and liquid specific volumes, Lf${{L}_{\mathrm{f}}}$ is the latent heat of fusion, and κ l is the liquid isothermal compressibility. Π0${{\it{\Pi}}_0}$ ranks materials and guides supercooling design for negative-Clapeyron-slope substances. For water, Π0${{\it{\Pi}}_0}$ ≈ 0.048. Cryoprotectants increase it several-fold, suppressing nucleation beyond colligative freezing-point depression.
